religiosity, social class, and gender are significant predictors of positive attitudes toward various aspects of school, with the effects of religiosity and gender being more powerful than that of social class.

religiosity, as indicated either by self-reported frequency or church attendance or personal prayer, was a significant predictor of more positive attitudes toward school in general and toward specific subjects such as English, music, mathematics, games, religious education, school assemblies, and school itself.

the influence of religion on attitudes toward school among 11-year-old children in England.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
religious pupils are more likely to have more favorable attitudes toward their schools than are pupils who are not religious.
religiously oriented individuals, particularly those who are female, are more likely to be favorably disposed toward school and its component parts.
religiosity, gender, and socioeconomic status have a significant impact on attitudes toward school, but not toward games lessons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more religious people are, the more they are likely to hold positive attitudes toward school.
the more often a student goes to church, the more likely he or she is to like school and to like school subjects, especially religious education and music lessons.
religiosity is a positive predictor of school attitudes and school performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
religion and religiosity are associated with positive attitudes toward school.
the more religious people are, the more they tend to value school and education.
we need to be aware of the influence of social class and gender on children’s attitudes toward different aspects of schooling.
